arrivalEssentials: Confirm your visa or e-visa status before travel and keep the approval details accessible.
Use Grab or a reputable taxi for the cleanest first transfer out of the airport.
Carry small VND notes for transport, snacks, and places that are still cash-first.
Set up mobile data quickly if you plan to navigate busy city areas on arrival.

options.bestFor: Simple app-based pickup and a clearer fare before you leave
options.notes: A reliable first option if you want to avoid haggling or language friction.

options.bestFor: Direct transfer when you want an easy curbside ride
options.notes: Use reputable companies and confirm the meter or fixed-fare approach before departure.

entryRequirements.passportValidity: Carry at least 6 months passport validity beyond arrival.
entryRequirements.visaSummary: Australian passport holders should not assume visa-free entry; check whether you need an e-visa or another permission for your travel purpose and dates.
entryRequirements.arrivalCardOrDeclaration: Vietnam does not currently use a general digital arrival card for typical visitors, but you should confirm the official visa or e-visa process and any current entry formalities before boarding.
entryRequirements.officialSourceNote: Use the official Vietnam immigration portal for visa and entry checks rather than third-party visa sites.
importantNotes: Keep a digital and printed copy of any visa approval or reference number you receive.
Arrival procedures and permitted stay lengths should be verified directly against the current official rules.

handyPhrases.context: Useful in shops, hotels, and cafes.
Helpful at markets or informal food stalls.

businessEtiquette.summary: Vietnamese business culture often appreciates respect, patience, and a willingness to build trust before pushing for fast closure.
tips: Use both hands when offering a business card or document where practical.
Expect some meetings to begin with relationship-building conversation.
Keep criticism private and phrased carefully.
Avoid pressing for immediate agreement before the relationship feels settled.
Written follow-up helps confirm decisions when meetings feel polite but non-committal.

foodAndPracticalities.tapWater: Do not use tap water for drinking; bottled or properly filtered water is the safer choice.
foodAndPracticalities.tipping: Tipping is not universal, but it is increasingly common in tourist-friendly restaurants, spas, and private transport.
foodAndPracticalities.dietaryNotes: Fish sauce is common, so vegetarian travellers should ask clearly rather than assume a dish is meat-free.
foodAndPracticalities.commonFoodTips: Street food can be excellent, but choose busy stalls and watch how fresh ingredients are handled.

moneyAndPayments.cardAcceptance: Cards are common in hotels and larger cafes, but cash still matters in many everyday situations.
moneyAndPayments.cashNotes: Have smaller notes for taxis, convenience purchases, and local eateries.
moneyAndPayments.tipping: Optional but increasingly common for good service in tourist-facing areas.
roughCostExamples: Beer at a casual bar or restaurant: about VND 30000 to 70000 (AUD 2 to 4)
Simple local meal: about VND 50000 to 120000 (AUD 3 to 6)
Grab from SGN to District 1: about VND 120000 to 250000 (AUD 6 to 13)

localTransportApps.notes: Usually the easiest first-day transport tool in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi.

localTransportApps.name: Google Maps
localTransportApps.notes: Helpful for judging whether a short ride is worth it in heavy traffic.

emergencyNumbers.label: Police, ambulance, and fire
notes: 113 is the police emergency number; local response lines can differ by service.
For medical or hotel-supported help, ask staff to place the call if language is a concern.
